subject: business-studies
title: Resistance to Change
welcome_lead: Why people resist and how leaders overcome it.
meta_desc: A-Level Change: causes of resistance and tactics to overcome it.
final_note: Treat resistance as information - most resistance reveals real risks worth fixing.

concepts.def: Fear of losing status, pay or routine.
Resistance from missing or wrong information.
Honest disagreement about the plan's merits.

walkthroughs.body_html: Kotter and Schlesinger identify self-interest, misunderstanding, low trust, different assessments, low tolerance for change and habit. Diagnosing the cause shapes the right response.
Tactics range from education and participation at the cooperative end to negotiation, manipulation and coercion at the forceful end - each with costs and ethics.
Different assessments respond to data and dialogue. Self-interest may need negotiation. Speed crises may demand coercion, but at the cost of trust later.

mcqs.q: Resistance from missing information is best treated with:

options: Last resort with high cost to trust
